Among them were also impure people who came to worship the Lord from their places of residence. There were also people who were impure by birth, occupation, conduct, and so on. He had to be among them, touching them all. By touching such impure people, one becomes impure. This is called "theettu" (impurity). "Theettu" means "touching" and "viluppu" means "wound." Even today, we see these truths. Doctors who treat patients by touching them, after treating them, cleanse and purify themselves and the medical instruments they used, and then treat the next patients. This is a practice that doctors follow even today to avoid being affected by germs that come from touching impure people. Similarly, here, there are countless people who are impure in their minds and other inner instruments (karanas) due to differences in their karmic maturity. Thus, by touching many such people who are impure in their minds and other inner instruments, those who are more mature, by touching those who are less mature, it will harm the inner being of the mature ones through their outer instruments. This is a subtle state. That is why our elders say that one should associate with good people and avoid associating with bad people. Therefore, Naminandhi Adigal says that he has become impure by being touched by many different people who came together. Therefore, he should not enter the house or perform pujas without bathing. Therefore, he must bathe and purify himself before entering the house and performing Shiva Puja. Therefore, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar tells his wife, "Bring cool, good water and other things here for that." Therefore, the purification by bathing that Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar mentions here refers to both external and internal purification. External purification means bathing in cool water and so on. Internal purification means applying sacred ash (Thiruneeru), chanting mantras like Aghora, and so on. The Vedas and Agamas state that this should be done before beginning. Furthermore, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar says, "Bring cool, good water for bathing." Water suitable for bathing, water appropriate for bathing, is cool water. Bathing in hot water is a very recent custom. Therefore, the water should be cool. It should also be pure water that has not been contaminated. Therefore, he says, "Bring cool water and other things." Thus, Nayanar says, "Bring cool, good water, sacred ash, clean, dry clothes, earth, a japamala, and other things for purification." Nayanar arrived at night. Therefore, out of eagerness to complete the aforementioned duties and put her husband to sleep before midnight, Nayanar's wife quickly goes inside the house to fetch all the things Nayanar requested. Now, the next two verses, the 26th and 27th verses:

"At that time, whether by the grace of his Lord or by the fatigue of his body, we do not know, but without any delay, sleep came upon the pure devotee, and he slept, remembering the feet of the Lord of the celestials. While he was sleeping, in his dream, Veethi Vidanga Peruman of Thiruvārūr, as if coming for the worship of the loving devotee, came and blessed him, saying, 'You will see that all those born in Thiruvārūr, the knowledgeable Brahmins, are our Ganas.' Then he disappeared from there." These verses are very important in explaining the Puranam of Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar. We will continue to reflect. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Swamigal's Periya Puranam, Part 536, Thirunindrachcharukkam, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar Puranam. Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar's wife quickly goes inside the house to fetch the items needed for Nayanar to bathe and purify himself. Not only does she go quickly, but she also prepares all the items and returns quickly. While she is doing this, a divine event occurs. In this short interval, Nayanar falls asleep. He falls into a slumber. Sekkizhar Peruman states that he does not know whether this was due to the grace of the Lord or the fatigue of Nayanar's long walk. However, Nayanar falls asleep. Even though Sekkizhar Peruman states this, it is concluded that Nayanar fell asleep due to the grace of God. This is because Nayanar was looking forward to bathing and performing the puja. His wife had gone inside the house to fetch clean water. In this situation, Nayanar would not normally fall asleep. But due to divine grace, Nayanar quickly falls asleep for a short while. The sleep that Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar experienced was not ordinary sleep or slumber. It was not the kind of sleep that causes delusion. It was not like the sleep that comes to us. Nayanar experienced the state called "Minmala Avasthai." This is not like our sleep. Therefore, Nayanar enters such a state. Even in that state of sleep, which is different from wakefulness, great souls are those who worship God without forgetting Him. That is the nature of great souls. The same thing happens to Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar here. While Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar is sleeping, he has a dream. In that dream, Thiruvārūr Peruman, Veethi Vidanga Peruman, appears. How does He appear? He appears as if coming for Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar's puja. Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar is about to bathe, purify himself, and perform puja. Thyagaraja Peruman, Veethi Vidanga Peruman, appears in his dream as if coming to accept the puja. This indicates that Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar regularly worshipped Thyagaraja Peruman as the Lord of his inner worship (Athmaartha Puja) in his daily puja. It also indicates that Thyagaraja Peruman regularly came to accept the puja performed by Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar. God is omnipresent. One must make a request to God to be present in one's puja and remain there for the duration of the puja in the Linga form. God accepts this and grants it. These are the rules of Shiva Puja according to the Shivagamas. Therefore, the Lord, who is about to appear for the puja that Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar is about to perform, appears in Nayanar's dream.

Thus, appearing in his dream, the Lord blesses Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar, saying, "All those born in Thiruvārūr are knowledgeable Brahmins (Gnana Maraiyorgal). They are all our Shiva Ganas. You will see that they are indeed our Shiva Ganas." Thyagaraja Peruman says this to Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar in his dream. Therefore, all those born in Thiruvārūr are knowledgeable Brahmins, and they are all Shiva Ganas. This is stated in the first verse of Thandiyadigal Nayanar Puranam: "The greatness of those born in Thiruvārūr is due to their penance." Therefore, those souls who have attained the blessing of being born in Thiruvārūr are those who have performed penance in many previous births, attained knowledge, and are qualified to attain liberation (Mukti). Therefore, all those born in Thiruvārūr are knowledgeable Brahmins. Therefore, God tells Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar that they are capable of attaining liberation and becoming His Ganas. This is why Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praises those born in Thiruvārūr as collective devotees (Thogaiyadiyargal) in Thiruthondar Thogai, saying, "I am a servant to all those born in Thiruvārūr." This also explains that Thiruvārūr is a place where one attains liberation by being born there. Thus, God Thyagaraja Peruman appeared in Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar's dream, said this, and then disappeared. What happens after the Lord blesses him in this way is explained by Sekkizhar Peruman in the next verse:

"The Primal Lord appeared, and he awoke. Fearing that he had intended not to perform the night worship, he rose, worshipped, and told his wife what had happened. At dawn, he hurried to the Lord's Thiruvārūr, and as he approached the city, he saw all those born and living in divine Thiruvārūr, who, by the light of their eyes, became the form of Lord Manikandar, shining with abundant light. Seeing their bodies, he clasped his hands, bowed down in fear, fell to the ground, worshipped, and rejoiced greatly." Thyagaraja Peruman is the Primal Lord (Aadhi Devar), Shiva, the supreme God, the Lord of all Devas. Thiruvalluvadeva Nayanar also states in the Thirukkural, "The world begins with the Primal Lord." "Aadhi" means the ancient Lord who is the beginning and cause of everything. "He who appeared before everyone" is from Thirunavukkarasu Peruman's Thevaram. The first verse of Thiruthāndagam for Thiruvālavai is "O Lord, I am your servant from now on." "Is it not so?" is from Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's Thiruvēnnainallur Thevaram. "The knower is the first aphorism of Sivagnanabodham." Therefore, after Thyagaraja Peruman, the Primal Lord, appeared in Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar's dream, revealed that all those born in Thiruvārūr are knowledgeable Brahmins and His Ganas, and said, "I will show you that truth, and you will see it," and then disappeared, meaning that He withdrew the form He showed in the dream into His own true nature. This is because if God had continued to appear in the dream without withdrawing Himself, Nayanar would have continued to delight in that state. The night would have passed, and Nayanar would have deviated from his daily ritual of worshipping his soul's Lord at the appropriate time at night. That is why the Lord withdraws the form He showed in the dream into His true nature. Even worshipping God in a dream is a form of worship. However, the Lord wished for Nayanar to attain the blessing of worshipping in both dream and waking states. That is also why the Lord withdraws from the dream. Even this withdrawal is an act of God's grace. Therefore, the Lord wished for Nayanar to realize that all those born in Thiruvārūr are Shiva Ganas. Nayanar realized this. Souls can only realize through God's grace. One can only see if God shows. "Who can see the Lord with the eye on His forehead if He does not show?" is a Thevaram verse by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. "By His grace, we worship His feet" is from Thiruvachakam, Sivapuranam. "Just as the mind shows to the seeing eye, so does the mind show by seeing" is the eleventh aphorism of Sivagnanabodham. Therefore, the Lord wished for Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar to realize this truth. Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar also realized it accordingly. Therefore, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar rises, fearing that he was about to commit the sin of offending Shiva. What was the sin? If Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar had bathed and then gone inside to perform puja as he had initially intended, two types of sins might have occurred. He would have failed to worship the Lord of his soul at the appropriate time at night. He also considered the holy assembly of devotees in Thiruvārūr, who are Shiva Ganas, as an impure crowd. That sin would also have been incurred.

Thus, two sins would have occurred if God had not blessed him in this way. Therefore, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar rises, fearing that he was about to commit the sin of offending Shiva. He rises while still worshipping. After rising, he goes inside and performs puja without bathing and purifying himself. He begins the puja in the same state as he woke up, without even performing a water ritual. Generally, if we sleep normally, after waking up, it is appropriate to purify ourselves, bathe, refresh ourselves, and then begin the puja or ritual. But the sleep that Nayanar experienced was a sleep that allowed him to witness a sacred vision. Therefore, if he had bathed after witnessing this sacred vision, it would have been like washing away the dream vision. Therefore, he rose directly from the sacred vision he had seen, and without performing any purification, he went inside and worshipped in the same state. He performed the puja. Thus, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar tells his wife what God had blessed him with. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar's wife as "Madharar" in this verse. "Madhar" means woman. Sekkizhar Peruman uses the honorific plural "Madharar" here, because Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar's wife not only supported her husband in his worldly life but also in his spiritual life. Therefore, when her husband, tired from his journey, tried to sleep outside the house, she woke him up and requested him to perform Shiva Puja, the daily ritualistic sacrifice (nithya velvi) as an ancillary part of it, then partake of the sacred food, and then go to sleep. Therefore, Nayanar's wife is not only his beloved in body but also in soul. That is why Sekkizhar Peruman refers to her as "Madharar" instead of "Madhar." Thus, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar tells his wife exactly what happened in the dream. We will continue to reflect. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Swamigal's Periya Puranam, Part 537, Thirunindrachcharukkam, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar Puranam. Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar tells his wife about the message the Lord conveyed in his dream and then, at dawn, quickly goes to the Lord's Thiruvārūr. It is stated here, "He saw that city as he approached the Lord's Thiruvārūr." "Nadhanartham Thiruvārūr" indicates that Thiruvārūr is the Lord Shiva's wealth, a city filled with the wealth of liberation (Mukti). "Aarthal" means to be filled. Since the wealth of liberation (Thiru) is abundant here, it is called Thiruvārūr. All those born in Thiruvārūr are knowledgeable Brahmins (Gnana Maraiyorgal) and Shiva Ganas. Therefore, all those born in Thiruvārūr are the possessions of Lord Shiva, His wealth. Such a city, filled with wealth, is Thiruvārūr. Therefore, as he approaches the city of Thiruvārūr, he sees the city in the distance. As soon as he sees the city from afar, Nayanar prostrates himself. As he gets closer, he sees the people living in Thiruvārūr, those born in Thiruvārūr. As he gets even closer, they all appear as Shiva Ganas. Sekkizhar Peruman sings that all those born and living in Thiruvārūr, who live by the principle that the purpose of life is to worship Shiva and His devotees without forgetting them, have attained Shivasaaroopam (the form of Shiva). Here, Sekkizhar Peruman does not say "all those born in Thiruvārūr," which would include everyone born there, but "all those born and living in Thiruvārūr." Therefore, even if one is born in Thiruvārūr, if one does not live a life of worshipping Shiva and His devotees without forgetting them, they have not attained the purpose of life. Therefore, they would not fall within this category. Thus, all those born and living in Thiruvārūr who follow the path of Shiva appear to Nayanar's eyes as having attained Shivasaaroopam. Shivasaaroopam is a state that comes as a result of Shivayoga. It is a stage before great souls who have mastered Shivayoga attain Gnanam and Shivasaayujyam (union with Shiva). Those who live by the path of Chariyai attain the state of Saalokam (residing in Shiva's world). Those who live by the path of Kiriyai attain the state of Saameepam (being near Shiva). Those who live by the path of Shivayoga attain the state of Shivasaaroopam. Such great souls who have attained Shivasaaroopam are about to attain Gnanam and Shivasaayujyam. Such great people are those who are born and live in Thiruvārūr. Therefore, they all appear as having attained Shivasaaroopam, as luminous forms, as forms of light in Shiva's light, as the light of Shiva Gnanam. By virtue of being born in Thiruvārūr, they are destined to attain Shivasaaroopam and Mukti in due course. Therefore, in accordance with the Lord's words in the dream, "All those born in Thiruvārūr are knowledgeable Brahmins; I will show them to you, and you will see them," Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar, who has now arrived in Thiruvārūr, sees them all as having attained Shivasaaroopam, as luminous forms. Upon seeing this vision, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar raises his hands in worship, prostrates himself on the ground, and is filled with great joy. After this, the vision disappears. That is, the Lord, who showed everyone in Thiruvārūr as having attained Shivasaaroopam, now withdraws that vision. Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar immediately requests forgiveness for his mistake and worships. Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar had gone to worship the Lord of Thiruvārūr in Thirumani. There, he thought that he had become impure by touching people of various castes who had gathered together. He therefore thought he needed to bathe and purify himself. Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar requests the Lord to forgive all such mistakes. Thereafter, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar leaves his village and settles in Thiruvārūr. Nayanar considered living in Thiruvārūr as a great life. In addition, he continues to perform services for the Lord and His devotees in Thiruvārūr. He performs sacred services to ensure that the daily (nithya) and occasional (naimithika) rituals, as we discussed earlier, are properly observed. He performs sacred services such as Chariyai (external worship). He also performs services for devotees. He has been performing the sacred service of providing whatever is needed for a long time to the devotees of Shiva who apply sacred ash (Thiruneeru). Due to this greatness and distinction, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman praises Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar in his Thiruppathikam as "the pure gold (aani pon) among the devotees of the Lord who dwells in the anthill (Puttidam Konda Nadhar), who resides in the beautiful anthill." Gold is inherently precious. The instrument used to measure its purity is called a touchstone (urai aani). Similarly, Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar is the one who measures the devotion of great devotees. This is why Thirunavukkarasu Peruman refers to him as "Thondarkku Aani" in his Thiruppathikam. "The Lord's devoted servant, Naminandhi, who lights lamps, is like pure gold among the devotees, and his service is known throughout the world, especially during the Panguni Uthiram festival in Thiruvārūr." This verse is the second verse of the 102nd Thiruppathikam of the 4th Thirumurai, which belongs to the Thiruvārūr temple. Just like Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, Thirugnanasambandha Peruman also praises Naminandhi Adigal in his Thevaram:

"The Lord who is beyond comprehension, whom even Brahma and Vishnu could not find, who is worshipped by Naminandhi, the great devotee who controls his breath and meditates on the Lord with the beautiful eye, is the Lord of Kozhili, who is adorned with flowers." This is a verse by Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, the 6th verse of the 62nd Thiruppathikam of the 1st Thirumurai, which belongs to the Thirukkōḷili temple. Thus, the character and intense love of Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar are spoken of. Now, Sekkizhar Peruman composes the concluding verse:

"In this manner, Naminandhi Adigal, whose goodness grew, performed many sacred services that all worlds worshipped, and attained a place in the beautiful radiant light that grows in the shade of the feet of the King of Thiruvārūr, who comes with the moon on his head and the river in his matted locks." Thus, Sekkizhar Peruman sings in the concluding verse that Naminandhi Adigal, whose goodness grew, performed many sacred services that all worlds worshipped, and attained a place in the beautiful radiant light that grows in the shade of the feet of Thyagaraja Peruman of Thiruvārūr. Nayanar worshipped Thyagaraja Peruman, the King of Thiruvārūr, as his soul's Lord. Therefore, he merged with the light of Shiva at the feet of that Lord. The shade of the feet is mentioned because it removes the heat of birth. The radiant light that grows at the feet is mentioned because it removes the darkness of ignorance, which is the root impurity (Moola Malam) of ego (Aanavam). It is customary to metaphorically refer to the feet in this way. Thus, Sekkizhar Peruman concludes the Puranam of Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar by singing that Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar attained a place in the beautiful radiant light that grows in the shade of the feet of Thyagaraja Peruman. Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar is the last Nayanar in this chapter called Thirunindrachcharukkam. Thus, Sekkizhar Peruman concludes the Puranam of Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar and blesses us. This chapter, Thirunindrachcharukkam, is based on the fourth verse of Thiruthondar Thogai, "Thirunindra Chemmaiye Chemmaiya Konda." According to "I am a servant to the devotees of Perunambi Kulachchirai," Sekkizhar Peruman narrates the Puranam of Kulachchirai Nayanar. According to "I am a servant to Perumizhalai Kurumbar and Peyar," he narrates the Puranam of Perumizhalai Kurumba Nayanar and Karaikkal Ammaiyar. According to "I am a servant to Appoodhi Adigal," he narrates the Puranam of Appoodhi Adigal Nayanar. According to "I am a servant to Neelanakkar of Saththamangai, surrounded by clear water," he narrates the Puranam of Thiruneelanakka Nayanar. According to "I am a servant to Arunanambi Naminandhi Adigal," Sekkizhar Peruman narrates the Puranam of Naminandhi Adigal Nayanar, following the verses sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal in Thiruthondar Thogai. In addition, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal concludes this fourth verse with "Arooran is a servant to the Lord of Aroor." Accordingly, Nambiandar Nambigal composes a verse in Thiruthondar Thiruvandhadhi. Similarly, at the end of this chapter, Sekkizhar Peruman also composes a eulogy for Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. "Arooran is a servant to the Lord of Aroor" is the concluding phrase in Thiruthondar Thogai. In this fourth verse, which begins with "Thirunindra," seven devotees are mentioned. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal concludes this fourth verse by saying that he, Arooran, is a servant to these seven devotees individually and also to the Lord of Thiruvārūr. Accordingly, Nambiandar Nambigal composes a eulogy for Sundaramoorthy Swamigal at this point in Thiruthondar Thiruvandhadhi. That verse is as follows:

"He who sang incomparable Tamil hymns for Nandi, our Lord, and the Lord of Thiruvārūr, and who attained the grace of His feet, which are difficult to contemplate in the flowing waters of the Kaveri, and who worships those very feet, is called Vanthondar in this world." Thus, Nambiandar Nambigal praises Sundaramoorthy Swamigal in the genre work Thiruthondar Thiruvandhadhi. In accordance with this genre work, Sekkizhar Peruman also concludes this chapter with a eulogy for Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. Similarly, at the end of every chapter, Sekkizhar Peruman concludes with a eulogy for Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. This is the structure Sekkizhar Peruman adopted. "Arooran is a servant to the Lord of Aroor" is the concluding phrase of Thiruthondar Thogai in every verse. Accordingly, at the end of each chapter of Periya Puranam, Sekkizhar Peruman includes a eulogy for Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. Therefore, the concluding verse of this chapter is the 1898th verse, which is a eulogy for Sundaramoorthy Swamigal in Periya Puranam. That verse is as follows:

"He who, in ancient times, on a good day, rescued a young Brahmin boy, whose chest was adorned with the five-weapon amulet, from the mouth of a lone great crocodile in the lotus pond of Thiruppukkozhiyur, those who remember his feet will be rescued from the cycle of birth and death." This is the concluding verse of Thirunindrachcharukkam in Periya Puranam, a eulogy for Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. Its meaning is as follows: Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, also known as Aludaiya Nambigal, rescued a young Brahmin boy, who had died on a previous day and whose chest was adorned with the five-weapon amulet, from the mouth of a lone great crocodile in the lotus pond of Thiruppukkozhiyur (Avinashi). Those who remember the feet of such a Sundaramoorthy Swamigal will be rescued from the cycle of birth and death. Sekkizhar Peruman praises Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, saying that just as Sundaramoorthy Swamigal brought back the Brahmin boy who had been swallowed by the crocodile in Avinashi temple after a long time, so too will Sundaramoorthy Swamigal rescue souls from the mouth of this birth, which clings relentlessly like a crocodile. Sekkizhar Peruman praises the feet of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, saying that those who remember those feet will be rescued from the mouth of this birth. Thus, Sekkizhar Peruman concludes the fifth chapter of Periya Puranam, Thirunindrachcharukkam, by praising the feet of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. We have completed five chapters out of the total thirteen chapters in Periya Puranam. We have reflected on the Puranams of 26 Nayanmars out of the total 63 Nayanmars. We have reflected on the Puranam of one collective devotee out of the nine collective devotees. Out of the total 4281 verses, we have completed reflecting on 1898 verses so far. The grace of our Lord, the grace of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, the grace of Nambiandar Nambigal, and the grace of Sekkizhar Peruman have enabled us to complete this reflection. Without the grace of God and the Guru, such a magnificent Gnana Puja would not be possible. Therefore, we praise and worship the grace of the Guru and the grace of God who have bestowed this Gnana Puja upon us. Thus, we conclude this chapter, Thirunindrachcharukkam, and are now going to reflect on the sixth chapter, Vambara Varivanda Charukkam. In that, we are going to reflect on the sacred history of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman. Therefore, we thank the Guru and God who have made this reflection possible so far, and we pray to the Guru and God that we may attain the blessing of reflecting on the Puranam of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman in Vambara Varivanda Charukkam and the Puranams of the remaining Nayanmars. We will continue to reflect. Thiruchitrambalam.
